data.narrative:
World Labs, founded by Fei-Fei Li and three co-founders, is a Series A artificial intelligence and software company that has raised $1.23B to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and eight private firms operating in AI and software at Series A or adjacent stages. Key private comparables include Reflection AI, Scale AI, Physical Intelligence, Black Forest Labs, and Field AI.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $1.2B total raised as a proxy base value and applies a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the next financing stage, yielding $2.5B. Peer-median analysis examines five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $5.6B, though the peer set ranges from $2.0B (Field AI, Series B) to $29.0B (Scale AI, Series B), indicating substantial dispersion in the market.

These methods triangulate to a valuation range of $2.1B (low) to $6.4B (high), with a median of $4.0B. The wide peer dispersion—a 14.5x spread between minimum and maximum—reflects meaningful uncertainty in AI software valuations at this stage. Key uncertainties include the applicability of later-stage Series B comparables to World Labs' current Series A position and heterogeneity in product maturity and revenue generation across the peer set.
